lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: portfolio curation and selection rationale

studentTask.text: Today's focus: portfolio curation and selection rationale. Essential question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to portfolio curation and selection rationale change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim? By the end of this lesson you should be able to: Explain what portfolio curation and selection rationale means and name the textual signal that tells you it is in play. You'll need: course notebook or digital equivalent; the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation; citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course.

guidedSupport.text:
Work through this with a facilitator, tutor, or on your own if you're ready:
- Preparation check: Confirm the learner has read and researched the material and arrives with located evidence. Unprepared participation is rescheduled, not penalised.
- Seminar: Discuss with prepared evidence and agreed collegial rules; the facilitator may still moderate turn-taking. The discussion is about today's lesson. The tutor may pose questions and challenge reasoning but does not supply positions.
- Disagreement log: Record the strongest point made against the learner's own position and what it would take to answer it.
- Private option: A private route is always available: at the learner's preference this seminar is held privately one-to-one with the facilitator, or submitted in writing. No group, public, or recorded participation is ever required.
- Reflection: Name one view you changed, qualified, or held with better reasons than before.

If you get stuck:
- If prerequisite gap: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for today's lesson, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
- If repeated error pattern: Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of today's lesson.
- If procedure without understanding: Ask the learner to explain why the move for today's lesson works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.

independentEvidenceTask.text: Participate in or write out a seminar on today's lesson with prepared, located evidence. When finished: State the strongest point made against your position and your best answer to it.
